t: In addition to the amounts otherwise provided by section 101, an additional amount is provided for “Federal Communications Commission—Salaries and Expenses” for consumer education associated with the transition to digital television occurring on February 17, 2009, at a rate for operations of $20,000,000.

fable.w: This section only appropriates additional funds to the FCC for consumer education about the digital television transition. The tempting reading is that "consumer education" involves the public, but it is one-way outreach from the government, not consultation with or input from outside parties before a federal decision. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue is created.
fable.s: an additional amount is provided for “Federal Communications Commission—Salaries and Expenses” for consumer education associated with the transition to digital television

opus.w: This section only adds funding to the FCC's salaries-and-expenses account for consumer education about the digital television transition. Educating consumers is one-way outreach from the agency to the public. It does not involve consulting outside parties before a federal decision, so it does not count as participation, even though the public is involved.
opus.s: an additional amount is provided for “Federal Communications Commission—Salaries and Expenses” for consumer education associated with the transition to digital television
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** "Consumer education" for the digital television transition involves the public, so it could look like public participation. That fails because education goes one way, from the FCC to consumers. Nobody outside the government is consulted, comments, sits on a board, or gets a say in a federal decision. The section is only an appropriation, adding funds at a set rate for operations.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriation provision that authorizes funding for the Federal Communications Commission to conduct consumer education. It does not require the FCC to consult with, coordinate with, or seek input from any outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The definition of participation requires consultation or coordination with people outside the government before a decision is made, which is not present here.
qwen_chat.s: an additional amount is provided for “Federal Communications Commission—Salaries and Expenses” for consumer education associated with the transition to digital television occurring on February 17, 2009, at a rate for operations of $20,000,000.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "consumer education" implies interacting with the public, thus constituting participation. However, the text only authorizes funding for the FCC to conduct this education; it does not mandate that the FCC consult with, coordinate with, or seek input from the public or any outside entity before making a decision. The activity is one-way (government to public) and administrative, not participatory in the sense of the definition (consultation/coordination before a decision).
